lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Pronounce common lunch words and greet a server or a local diner politely.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Greet a server, say your name, and say three lunch words like chile, tortilla and arroz clearly.
lessons.title: Lunch Greetings and French Sounds
lessons.objective: Greet lunch staff politely, introduce yourself, and say common lunch words clearly in French.
lessons.focus: Use bonjour and vous with an unfamiliar server. Hear é in café, French u in jus, the nasal vowel in pain, and the silent final t in poulet.
lessons.scene: Sam enters a small lunch counter in Lyon and asks Camille for the menu.

cards.note: In a restaurant, la carte lists dishes; un menu can mean a set meal.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonjour. Excusez-moi.
reader.en: Hello. Excuse me.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bonjour ! Bienvenue.
reader.en: Hello! Welcome.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Je m'appelle Sam. La carte, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: My name is Sam. The menu, please.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Oui, voici la carte.
reader.en: Yes, here is the menu.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Je vois du riz, du poulet et du pain.
reader.en: I see rice, chicken, and bread.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Il y a aussi de l'eau, du jus et du café.
reader.en: There is also water, juice, and coffee.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Merci beaucoup. Le jus, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: Thank you very much. The juice, please.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bien sûr. Bon appétit !
reader.en: Of course. Enjoy your meal!

speaking.goal: Greet the server with vous, say your name, ask for the menu, and pronounce café, jus, pain, and poulet.

recall.cueEnglish: From memory, get the server's attention.

hear.cueEnglish: Listen for the French word for bread.

type.cueEnglish: Type the French word for juice.

say.cueEnglish: Introduce yourself to the server in French.

write.cueEnglish: Write a polite request for the menu.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say numbers, prices in pesos, times and simple food quantities when ordering lunch.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell a counter worker how many of you there are, order 5 tacos, and check the price in pesos.
lessons.title: People, Portions, Euros and Time
lessons.objective: Give a group size, order counted lunch items, confirm a price in euros, and state an arrival time.
lessons.focus: Count from zéro through dix, cent and mille. Use nous sommes for group size, deux menus for counted items, un verre d'eau for quantity, and à midi et demi for 12:30. Euro amounts use euros after the number.
lessons.scene: Sam phones a lunch counter to order ahead for four friends and confirm their arrival time and total.

cards.en: Does that come to twenty-five euros?

cards.fr: Nous arrivons à midi et demi.
cards.en: We arrive at half past noon.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonjour. Nous sommes quatre.
reader.en: Hello. There are four of us.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Bonjour. Vous arrivez à quelle heure ?
reader.en: Hello. What time are you arriving?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Nous arrivons à midi et demi.
reader.en: We arrive at half past noon.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Très bien. Vous prenez quoi ?
reader.en: Very good. What will you have?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Deux menus et trois sandwichs, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: Two set meals and three sandwiches, please.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Et pour boire ?
reader.en: And to drink?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Une bouteille d'eau et un verre d'eau.
reader.en: A bottle of water and a glass of water.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Ça fait vingt-cinq euros.
reader.en: That comes to twenty-five euros.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Ça fait vingt-cinq euros ? Vous avez la monnaie ?
reader.en: Does that come to twenty-five euros? Do you have change?

speaking.goal: Say there are four of you, order two set meals and three sandwiches, give the 12:30 arrival time, and confirm the euro total.

see.cueEnglish: Find the phrase for four people in your group.

recall.cueEnglish: Recall how to say half past noon.

hear.cueEnglish: Listen for the quantity a bottle of water.

type.cueEnglish: Type two set meals in French.

say.cueEnglish: Tell the server that there are four of you.

write.cueEnglish: Write a question confirming the twenty-five-euro total.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say what food and places are like and where they are, using ser and estar.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Ask a server if a table is free and if the salsa is spicy, then say the food is delicious.
lessons.title: Describe Food and Find a Table
lessons.objective: Ask whether a table is free, describe a dish's taste and temperature, and locate a nearby place.
lessons.focus: French uses être for both description and current condition: la soupe est chaude, la sauce est épicée. Use il y a for availability and se trouve or est for location; Spanish ser/estar is source context, not a French verb contrast.
lessons.scene: Sam checks a table and a lunch dish before meeting a friend near the market.

cards.en: The market is very close by.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonjour. Cette table est libre ?
reader.en: Hello. Is this table free?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Oui, elle est libre. L'autre table est occupée.
reader.en: Yes, it is free. The other table is taken.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: La sauce est épicée ?
reader.en: Is the sauce spicy?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Oui, elle est épicée. La soupe est chaude aussi.
reader.en: Yes, it is spicy. The soup is hot too.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Je prends la soupe. C'est délicieux !
reader.en: I'll have the soup. It's delicious!

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Vous cherchez autre chose ?
reader.en: Are you looking for anything else?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Oui. Le marché est loin ?
reader.en: Yes. Is the market far?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Non, le marché est tout près. Il est ouvert.
reader.en: No, the market is very close by. It is open.

speaking.goal: Ask whether a table is free and whether the sauce is spicy; describe the soup's temperature and taste; ask where the market is.

see.cueEnglish: Find the question asking whether this table is free.

recall.cueEnglish: Recall the French adjective for spicy sauce.

hear.cueEnglish: Listen for the statement that the soup is hot.

type.cueEnglish: Type the French question asking if the sauce is spicy.

say.cueEnglish: Ask the server whether this table is free.

write.cueEnglish: Write that the market is very close by.

Source lesson 3 teaches Spanish ser/estar. French lesson 3 instead teaches être for description/condition and French availability/location expressions; verify this progression and naturalness with a qualified French reviewer.
